title: Measuring a rain garden
bodyMd:
In a fictional school, pupils planted a rain garden to collect water from a roof. During the first month, almost no water reached the overflow drain. The pupils initially claimed the garden could handle any storm. Their teacher asked them to compare that month’s rainfall with earlier records. It had been unusually dry, and no intense storm had occurred.

The pupils revised their claim. They could say the garden had worked under the observed conditions, but not that its capacity was unlimited. They installed a simple gauge and recorded both rainfall and overflow after later storms. The teacher did not treat the original enthusiasm as a mistake to be punished. It had supplied a question; the records would help turn that question into a defensible account of performance.
